inline_comments.comment: Per project changeset conventions, the first word of the description after the type prefix must be capitalized. Change `feat: implement` to `feat: Implement`.

`genColor` calls `configApi.getConfig()` here, and `getStyles` (its caller) also calls `configApi.getConfig()` at line 31. The project rule is to call `getConfig()` once at the entry point and pass the result down. Refactor `genColor` to accept the already-resolved `config` (or just `{ themeVariables, look }`) as a parameter instead of re-fetching it.

The loop bound is `options.THEME_COLOR_LIMIT` (always 12 in current themes), but the guard above only confirms `borderColorArray.length > 0` — not that it has exactly 12 entries. If any theme populates `borderColorArray` with fewer elements than `THEME_COLOR_LIMIT`, `borderColorArray[i]` will be `undefined` for the out-of-range indices, producing invalid CSS like `stroke: undefined;`. Cap the loop with `Math.min(options.THEME_COLOR_LIMIT, borderColorArray.length)` to make this defensive.

`fill: ${bkgColorArray?.length ? bkgColorArray[i] : ''};` produces `fill: ;` (an empty property value) when there is no background color array. An empty value is invalid CSS and browser handling is undefined — some browsers ignore the entire declaration block. Use `fill: none` as the fallback: `fill: ${bkgColorArray?.length ? bkgColorArray[i] : 'none'};`. The same issue appears on line 23 for the `rect` selector.

The selector `[data-look="${look}"][data-color-id="color-${i}"].node  rect` has two spaces between `.node` and `rect`. The equivalent `path` selector on line 16 uses a single space. Use a single space for consistency.
The `.edgeLabel` rule is indented with 4 spaces while every surrounding CSS rule in the same template literal uses 2-space indentation. Revert to 2-space indentation to match the rest of the file.

`.attr('viewBox', '0 0 25 20')` violates the project rule that `viewBox` must be set via the native DOM API because d3's `.attr()` can lowercase attribute names to `viewbox`, which SVG does not recognize, silently breaking the marker viewport. Use `markerSel.node().setAttribute('viewBox', '0 0 25 20')` on a saved reference to the marker selection. (Note: all existing markers in this file share this same pattern — those are also non-conformant — but the project rule still applies to new code.)

The divider previously received `attr('style', nodeStyles)`, so user-applied `style` statements (e.g., `style req_a fill:#f9f,...`) propagated to the divider line. Replacing that with `attr('class', 'divider')` means user-defined CSS styles no longer affect the divider for any look — including classic and handDrawn. If excluding divider from user styles is intentional for neo, scope the change: keep the original `attr('style', nodeStyles)` for non-neo and add the class-only path only for neo.

`requirementEdgeLabelBackground` is an edge-label background color — it is semantically unrelated to whether node path styles should be applied. Using it as a gate for applying `nodeStyles` to `.outer-path path` is misleading and fragile: a theme that omits `requirementEdgeLabelBackground` but has `borderColorArray` would still apply styles, making the condition's intent opaque. Simplify to just `nodeStyles && node.look !== 'handDrawn'` to make the intent clear: apply node inline styles whenever they exist and the look supports them.

general_comments.comment: No regression test covers the `handDrawn` look. The PR changes the divider-rendering branch (`rc.polygon` for neo, `rc.line` for else) and replaces the divider's inline style with a CSS class — both of which affect `handDrawn` paths. A Cypress `imgSnapshotTest` with `{ look: 'handDrawn' }` analogous to the existing classic regression test (bottom of the spec file) would confirm that handDrawn rendering is unaffected.

`nodeStyles` is applied twice to the requirement box: once on the roughjs wrapper `<g>` element via the pre-existing `rect.attr('class', 'basic label-container outer-path').attr('style', nodeStyles)`, and again on the `<path>` children inside that wrapper via the new `shapeSvg.selectAll('.outer-path path').attr('style', nodeStyles)`. Since child inline styles have higher specificity, the `<g>`-level application is now redundant. Consider removing `.attr('style', nodeStyles)` from the `rect.attr(...)` call to keep the styling responsibility in one place.
